text:
Fixed and verified. The bug was in `page_count` in `pager/paginate.py`: it used `total_items // per_page + 1`, which always adds an extra page when the item count is an exact multiple of `per_page` (9 items ÷ 3 = 3 pages, but the formula returned 4). That phantom 4th page made `has_next` true on the real last page and returned an empty list instead of raising.

The fix uses proper ceiling division — `(total_items + per_page - 1) // per_page` — with a special case returning 1 for an empty collection, preserving the documented "always at least 1 page" behavior. Verified: `paginate(range(9), 3, 3)` now reports `total_pages=3` with `has_next=False`, page 4 raises `ValueError`, non-multiple counts (10 items → 4 pages) and empty collections are unchanged, and the existing test suite passes.
